events.factual_description: The Hamilton Live and its authorized EVENTIM listing announce John K's Mystery Band for Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at The Hamilton Live in Washington, DC, with doors at 6:30 PM and the show at 8:00 PM. The authorized event page describes John Kadlecik as a DC-area singer, songwriter and guitarist, an original co-founder of Dark Star Orchestra, a former Furthur sideman to Phil Lesh and Bob Weir, and a musician currently performing with Melvin Seals & JGB. It also states that $5 from each ticket will be donated to DC Central Kitchen. The current page does not announce the additional Mystery Band personnel, so they are not inferred. The event copy mentions '2 nights,' but the current Hamilton calendar and exact EVENTIM series page list only November 25; only that verified date is recorded here.

en.why_it_matters: Kadlecik is part of the post-Garcia Dead lineage in a way that is unusually native to the DMV: he is a DC-area guitarist and singer who co-founded Dark Star Orchestra, then spent years inside Furthur with Phil Lesh and Bob Weir, while keeping improvisation at the center of his own work. A Mystery Band night at The Hamilton is therefore less interesting as repertory nostalgia than as a local branch of that improvisational language still being played by someone who helped carry it forward.
en.trip_verdict: Keep Thanksgiving Eve on the local board if the Dead-improvisation thread is calling. This is a good Washington night with a real regional connection, but with the supporting personnel still unannounced and Kadlecik active in several projects, I would fit it around rarer lineups, premieres, farewells or one-off contexts rather than move one of those to make room.

es.why_it_matters: Kadlecik forma parte del linaje post-Garcia de los Dead de una manera especialmente ligada al DMV: es guitarrista y cantante de la zona de DC, cofundó Dark Star Orchestra y después pasó años dentro de Furthur con Phil Lesh y Bob Weir, manteniendo la improvisación en el centro de su propio trabajo. Por eso una noche de Mystery Band en The Hamilton interesa menos como nostalgia de repertorio que como una rama local de ese lenguaje improvisatorio todavía tocada por alguien que ayudó a mantenerlo vivo.
es.trip_verdict: La tendría en el tablero local para la víspera de Thanksgiving si el hilo de improvisación de los Dead está llamando. Es una buena noche de Washington con una conexión regional real, pero con el resto de la banda todavía sin anunciar y Kadlecik activo en varios proyectos, la acomodaría alrededor de alineaciones más raras, estrenos, despedidas o contextos de una sola oportunidad en vez de mover uno de esos conciertos para hacerle espacio.
